approach: Records are append-only (records.rs header, D06; gate Rule::AppendOnly), so a merge cannot edit class B's file. A merge is a NEW `athena.failure-class/1` record with status `merged` that names the retired class (`merged_from`) and the surviving class (`merged_into`). In athena-data, `ClassStatus` gains `Merged { merged_into, merged_from }` (an old `"proposed"` string still parses), `FailureClass` gains `validate()` and `merged_into_class()`, and a `ClassMerges` type gives `resolve`, `is_retired` and `live_target` with cycle-safe chain following; `ClassMerges::of` does no sorting when the list holds no merge record. One shared rule, `introspect::class_named(classes, merges, name)`, finds the live class whose normalised name equals a given name (live or retired classes, merge records skipped). Both class-creation paths use it: `apply_answer` in introspect.rs (reuse instead of minting) and `Athena::review` in review.rs (`--new-class` refused with a pointer to the live class; `--class` refuses a merge record's id and a retired id, naming the target). Every reader that lists or counts classes reads through `ClassMerges`: registry reads (introspect.rs `read_records`, labeled.rs `read_inputs`) list only live classes and map case rows and labels to the target in memory; hestia `class_of`, the producer brief's `class_summaries`, `recurrence_vote` and `proposals::generate` resolve ids before comparing. `Athena::merge_classes(from, into)` is the library entry that checks and commits a merge record. No CLI command is added and the 158 existing records are not rewritten; both are marked design. The docs say plainly that creation-time reuse catches only names equal after normalising; differently worded duplicates still need a merge record.

decisions.choice: A merge is a new append-only FailureClass record (status merged, with merged_into and merged_from, fresh id), not an edit of the retired class's file. Readers fold the records into a retired-to-target map. If two merge records retire the same class, the earliest by (at, id) wins; merge_classes cannot write a cycle because its target must be live and not retired.
decisions.reason: records.rs:4 says a record is written once and never modified (D06); the gate's AppendOnly rule refuses a modified records/ file. A new record keeps history and still meets criterion 3's 'FailureClass with status merged and merged_into'. In a merge record, `proposed_by` is copied from the retired class only to keep the struct's shape; no introspection proposed the merge. The field's doc comment (introspection.rs line 304), defaults-loop.md 3.4 and D166 say so (answers finding 7). docs/records.md is not edited: line 107 is the class-label row and the file has no failure-class status text, so there is nothing to update (answers finding 4).

The variant makes 'merged without a target' unrepresentable. The code uses ClassStatus only as `ClassStatus::Proposed` and in assert_eq.

decisions.choice: Dedupe at creation through one shared helper `introspect::class_named(classes, merges, name) -> Option<RecordId>`: normalise both names with the existing `normalise`, skip merge records and empty normalised names, take the earliest match by (at, id), return its live target. `apply_answer` (model answer `new`) and `Athena::review` (`--new-class`) both call it. Introspect's `Records` keeps `all_classes: Vec<FailureClass>` and `merges: ClassMerges` and calls the helper on demand; no separate alias map.
decisions.reason: Creation is where the duplicates come from, and there are two creation paths (introspect.rs line ~1602 and review.rs line 287). The critic's finding 5 is right: review.rs compared names with `to_lowercase()`, a different rule, so 'Stale cache!' passed review while introspect would reuse 'stale cache'. One helper means one rule, enforced by code not prompt (user default 'mechanism').

rejected.why: Costs tokens on every sweep, is nondeterministic, can merge unlike classes, and defaults-loop.md line 753 lists Jev pairwise merging as not decided. It can follow later using the merge record.

rejected.option: Match by description or word overlap
rejected.why: No measured threshold; risks merging different causes. Exact normalised name is a rule that can be tested.

rejected.option: A manual-only merge with no creation check
rejected.why: Leaves the fault unfixed at its source; every new duplicate would need a person.

rejected.option: Change only introspect.rs and leave review.rs on its own rule
rejected.why: Leaves a second creation path that mints duplicates the first path would reuse.

decisions.choice: Be honest about reach: creation-time reuse catches only names equal after `normalise` (lower case, alphanumeric words). Model-written names for one cause often differ in wording, so differently worded duplicates still need a merge record. defaults-loop.md 3.4, the CHANGELOG entry and the D166 Tradeoff say this and name the follow-ups as design: count collisions with a backtest over the records branch, and add a user merge command.
decisions.reason: normalise (introspect.rs line 856) only lower-cases and splits into words. The 158-class problem is not claimed fixed; criterion 1 asks only for the normalised-name case (answers finding 6).

rejected.why: Not measurable here (records/ absent) and probably false for differently worded names.

decisions.choice: Resolve merges at read time, in memory. Registry reads list only live classes; case rows, labels and Jev choices map to the target. No record is rewritten. `ClassMerges::of` returns an empty map without sorting when there is no merge record; hestia `repeated_causes` builds it once and passes it to a private `class_of`, and `cause_key` (public) builds its own.
decisions.reason: Keeps records append-only and lets the 158 existing records stand. The empty-map fast path and the once-per-call build answer finding 8: no per-introspection re-sort.

risks.risk: Two introspections running at once both read the registry before either commits and both mint the same new name, giving one duplicate.
risks.mitigation: The check runs against the registry read at the start of each introspection, so later events dedupe against earlier ones; a rare same-moment pair is left for a merge record. Stated in the D166 Tradeoff.

risks.risk: ClassStatus loses Copy and gains a data variant; a use not seen (a copy of the field, a non-exhaustive match) fails to compile.
risks.mitigation: A workspace grep showed only `ClassStatus::Proposed` constructions and one assert_eq; `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` in criterion 4 catch the rest.

risks.risk: A request created for the retired class's id or name before the merge is no longer matched by hestia `mentions` once the cause key becomes the target's key, so a duplicate root-cause request could be queued.
risks.mitigation: `addressing_request` matches by cited introspection ids, which stay in the merged group, so the common case is covered. The text-only gap is listed in the D166 Tradeoff; the follow-up is for `mentions` to test every id that resolves to the target.

risks.risk: Name matching merges or reuses classes that differ only in punctuation or case but mean different things.
risks.mitigation: The rule is exact equality after `normalise`, the notion of equal text the code already uses for causes; the description is not compared; the earliest class wins deterministically.

risks.risk: The rule catches few real duplicates, because the model words one cause differently each time, and readers may take the 158-class problem as fixed.
risks.mitigation: Docs, CHANGELOG and D166 say plainly that only names equal after normalising are reused; the follow-ups (collision backtest over the records branch, user merge command) are named as design.

risks.mitigation: No code path writes a merge until this change has landed; drain rebuilds into the new binary after landing Athena's own code (D140). Stated in dependents.

risks.risk: No user command, so the merge path is unused in production until one is added.
risks.mitigation: Marked design in the changelog and section 3.4, and put to the user in an open question. `merge_classes` is tested end to end so a later command is thin.

risks.risk: Scope is wider than the nine listed deliverables (review.rs, briefs.rs, evidence_labels.rs, proposals.rs, cli review test), which risks a producer run that is too large.
risks.mitigation: Each extra edit is a few lines using the same `ClassMerges` or `class_named` helper, added after the core steps; each has a named test and a stated consequence if left out. The job brief's own deliverables are done first.

demonstrations.method: The three checks Athena runs, whole workspace, plus the refusal-corpus test as a regression. The rule added is a class-name match on model output and a review name check, not a parser, stem list, stop list or reading check, so no refusal_corpus.rs case maps to it and I cite none. The corpus run guards `cause_key`, which feeds generated root-cause requests (refusal_corpus.rs ~686-777 use introspections with failure_class None). Input forms of the new rule and the test that covers each: case difference, punctuation, extra spacing, boundary-reworded name, retired class's name, empty-after-normalising name, different wording (control) in the criterion 1 tests; `--new-class` with punctuation and case difference, merge-record id and retired id for `--class` in the criterion 2 review test; two existing live classes with equal normalised names pick the earliest by (at, id) in a `class_named` unit test.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.fails_without: A missed consumer fails the build: the ClassStatus change removes Copy and adds a variant, so any non-exhaustive match or copy use fails to compile; an unformatted file or a clippy warning fails the other commands.
demonstrations.seam: cargo itself. Existing `FailureClass { status: ClassStatus::Proposed, .. }` literals compile unchanged because no field is added.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff. defaults-loop.md section 3.4 gets a paragraph: creation (introspection and review) reuses a live or retired class with the same normalised name; a merge is an appended failure-class record with status merged naming the retired and surviving class; readers count a merged class under its target; `Athena::merge_classes` is built; creation-time reuse catches only names equal after normalising, so differently worded duplicates still need a merge record; the existing 158 classes are not rewritten by this change; a CLI merge command, a backtest counting collisions over the records branch, model-based clustering and the migration of existing classes are design (not built); a merge record's `proposed_by` is the retired class's and does not mean an introspection proposed the merge. The CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` `### Added` entry says the same. The policy test scans the new text for banned words and personal data.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- docs/design/defaults-loop.md CHANGELOG.md && cargo test -p xtask --test policy
demonstrations.observes: The statements (merge behavior, narrow reach, 158 classes not rewritten, unbuilt parts marked design) are present and the scan passes.
